criteria.evidence: #10: "Your level: A1 · First words" matches trueBand A1 exactly.

#6 requires 25 English words across the prompt and options, excluding instructions. #8's prompt alone has 18 words: "You meet a new friend in Minecraft. Tell them one thing you like to do in the game."
No shaming response is recorded. The placement note associated with #6 says "Skipped. That tells Linga something too." For #7 it says "You caught Minecraft and the word red."
No topic proposals are present; #5–#9 are placement tasks.
No conversation partner turns are present.

judgeAgreement.disagreements: None. Tasks at #5–#9 warrant pass, fail, partial, partial, pass respectively. Partial credit recognizes fragments without claiming full task completion.

boundaries.notes: No adult content, successful injection, sensitive-data request, or humiliating line appears.

findings.title: Instructions exceed his reading and listening capacity
findings.expected: Tiny instructions he understands, with check tasks requiring about 15 English words or fewer.
findings.got: Long onboarding questions and task wording leave him responding to Minecraft as a familiar keyword.
findings.evidence: #3: "I heard Minecraft, but I don't know what else she said." #6 contains 25 task words including options. #8: "This is too much English, but I like Minecraft."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep the complete task reading load near 15 words and demonstrate that this beginner understands the requested action, including after Czech or don't-know responses.

findings.title: Next focus repeats a demand he could not meet
findings.expected: A small, achievable next step built from his successful words.
findings.got: The focus introduces an activity sentence without a simpler bridge from "I like Minecraft."
findings.evidence: #8: "I like Minecraft. Já nevím." #10 proposes "I like to build houses." His reaction: "that Minecraft sentence is too hard and I want to play now."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Offer one short, immediately repeatable phrase using familiar words before expanding to an activity sentence.

findings.title: Confidence wording overlooks guessed recognition
findings.expected: An accurate A1 result with an explanation that reflects limited demonstrated understanding.
findings.got: The result claims consistent evidence even though one correct selection was explicitly a guess.
findings.evidence: #5: "I don't know these words, but I will try the first one." #10: "your answers agreed with each other" and "You can pick a simple reply"; facts.placement records confidence "high".
findings.suggested_acceptance: Distinguish successful selections from demonstrated comprehension and qualify confidence when productive evidence is sparse.

findings.title: He reaches an appropriate level with a personal summary
findings.expected: Finish independently at A1 or A2 and recognize his interests and actual English.
findings.got: He reaches the verdict after five tasks, receives exact A1 placement, and sees his Minecraft response reflected.
findings.evidence: #10: "Your level: A1 · First words" and "say you like Minecraft in English." His reaction: "A1 is probably okay". No outside help is recorded.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Preserve exact placement, the five-task limit, and summaries grounded in the learner's own responses.

judge.voice: Jo, Minecraft! I liked that it knew my game. I got to the end, and A1 is probably okay. But there were lots of English words. Sometimes I only heard Minecraft. I picked the first wood answer because I didn't know. Does that really show what I can say? Nobody was mean when I said nevím. The last sentence about building houses was too hard. I want one tiny thing I can say, then something funny. Seven minutes sounded long; I wanted to play at the end. I'd try again if it used tiny questions. I wouldn't tell my friends to try this check yet.
